description: The overall HGB average is taken over every lab record directly, so patients with more tests weigh more.

c.request: Among patients whose average hemoglobin (`HGB`) across their lab records (ignoring missing values) is above the overall average hemoglobin, list the patient ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the average of these above-average patients' averages. Show the top 10 by that last value, highest first, unrounded. The overall HGB average is taken over every lab record directly, so patients with more tests weigh more.
c.sql: WITH overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(HGB) as overall_hgb_avg FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL), patient_avgs AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) as patient_hgb_avg FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), above_avg_patients AS (SELECT pa.ID, pa.patient_hgb_avg, oa.overall_hgb_avg FROM patient_avgs pa, overall_avg oa WHERE pa.patient_hgb_avg > oa.overall_hgb_avg), above_avg_avg AS (SELECT AVG(patient_hgb_avg) as above_avg_patients_avg FROM above_avg_patients) SELECT aap.ID, aap.patient_hgb_avg, aap.patient_hgb_avg - aap.overall_hgb_avg as above_overall_avg, aap.patient_hgb_avg - aaa.above_avg_patients_avg as above_above_avg_avg FROM above_avg_patients aap, above_avg_avg aaa ORDER BY above_above_avg_avg DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For patients whose individual-patient average HGB (mean across non-null values per patient) exceeds the global average HGB (mean of all non-null HGB values across all laboratory records), show patient ID, their average HGB, their average HGB minus the global average HGB, and their average HGB minus the mean of all filtered patients' averages, sorted by the last metric descending, top 10 unrounded.
b.sql:
WITH global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(HGB) as global_avg_hgb
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL
),
patient_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(HGB) as patient_avg_hgb
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
filtered_patients AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.ID,
    pa.patient_avg_hgb,
    ga.global_avg_hgb
  FROM patient_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN global_avg ga
  WHERE pa.patient_avg_hgb > ga.global_avg_hgb
),
filtered_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(patient_avg_hgb) as filtered_patients_avg
  FROM filtered_patients
)
SELECT 
  fp.ID,
  fp.patient_avg_hgb,
  fp.patient_avg_hgb - fp.global_avg_hgb,
  fp.patient_avg_hgb - fa.filtered_patients_avg
FROM filtered_patients fp
CROSS JOIN filtered_avg fa
ORDER BY (fp.patient_avg_hgb - fa.filtered_patients_avg) DESC
LIMIT 10
b.raw: For patients whose individual-patient average HGB (mean across non-null values per patient) exceeds the global average HGB (mean of all non-null HGB values across all laboratory records), show patient ID, their average HGB, their average HGB minus the global average HGB, and their average HGB minus the mean of all filtered patients' averages, sorted by the last metric descending, top 10 unrounded.

d.request: Identify patients whose mean HGB across their laboratory records exceeds the arithmetic mean of all HGB values in the Laboratory table (where each record contributes one value, so patients with more tests weight the overall average more), then for each such patient report: patient ID, their mean HGB, their mean HGB minus the overall mean HGB, and their mean HGB minus the mean of all selected patients' mean HGBs, sorted by the last value descending, top 10 unrounded.
d.sql:
WITH overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(HGB) as overall_mean_hgb
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL
),
patient_means AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(HGB) as patient_mean_hgb
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
filtered_patients AS (
  SELECT 
    pm.ID,
    pm.patient_mean_hgb,
    os.overall_mean_hgb
  FROM patient_means pm
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE pm.patient_mean_hgb > os.overall_mean_hgb
),
selected_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(patient_mean_hgb) as mean_of_selected
  FROM filtered_patients
)
SELECT 
  fp.ID,
  fp.patient_mean_hgb,
  fp.patient_mean_hgb - fp.overall_mean_hgb as diff_from_overall,
  fp.patient_mean_hgb - ss.mean_of_selected as diff_from_selected_mean
FROM filtered_patients fp
CROSS JOIN selected_stats ss
ORDER BY diff_from_selected_mean DESC
LIMIT 10

a.request: For each patient ID in the Laboratory table, compute their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) over their lab records, ignoring missing values. Define the overall average as the mean `HGB` over all individual lab records pooled together, so each test counts once and patients with more tests weigh more. Keep the patients whose average is above that overall average. For each kept patient, list the ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the mean of the kept patients' averages. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest and show the top 10, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(HGB) as overall_average FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL), patient_avg AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) as patient_average FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), filtered_patients AS (SELECT pa.ID, pa.patient_average, oa.overall_average FROM patient_avg pa CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE pa.patient_average > oa.overall_average), kept_patients_mean AS (SELECT AVG(patient_average) as mean_of_kept FROM filtered_patients), final_result AS (SELECT fp.ID, fp.patient_average, fp.patient_average - fp.overall_average as above_overall, fp.patient_average - kpm.mean_of_kept as diff_from_kept_mean FROM filtered_patients fp CROSS JOIN kept_patients_mean kpm) SELECT ID, patient_average, above_overall, diff_from_kept_mean FROM final_result ORDER BY diff_from_kept_mean DESC LIMIT 10
